question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing across drug exposure
ideas.description: Introduce heritable random barcodes (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcode libraries) into a clonal population before treatment, then sequence barcodes in survivors and in pre-treatment cells. Matching barcodes between the two timepoints will show whether survivors come from a pre-existing subclone or arise de novo from drug-induced reprogramming.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment single-cell multiomics predicting survival
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) on untreated cells, then compare the profiles of cells that later survive versus die using a lineage-linked readout such as barcodes or live-cell photoconversion. Identifying transcriptional or chromatin-accessibility signatures that predict survival would reveal whether tolerance is primed before the drug is given.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporter tracking of individual fates
ideas.description: Use fluorescent reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell-cycle phase, ERK-KTR for pathway activity, and a drug-efflux or stress reporter) in time-lapse microscopy during drug exposure. Linking each cell's reporter state before and during treatment to its eventual death or survival will show which dynamic signaling or cell-cycle states confer tolerance.

ideas.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens with survival bottlenecks
ideas.description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi/a screens at high library coverage under a strong drug dose that kills most cells, then compare guide representation in survivors against untreated controls. Hits that enrich in survivors point to genes whose loss or gain is needed for tolerance, and comparing them with resistance screens from chronic exposure separates transient from stable mechanisms.

ideas.title: Chromatin and metabolic profiling of sorted survivors with reversibility tests
ideas.description: Sort or harvest surviving cells after a short drug pulse and profile their chromatin (CUT&Tag for H3K27ac/H3K4me3, ATAC-seq), metabolism (mitochondrial respiration, lipid and iron/ferroptosis markers), and proteome against bulk controls. Then test whether the survivor state is reversible by drug holidays and by inhibiting the implicated epigenetic or metabolic pathways, which distinguishes an adaptive epigenetic state from a fixed genetic one.
